paragraphs: Friend, here's what hits me about this passage. Pilate says Jesus is not guilty (Luke 23:14). Herod sends Him back, and Pilate says so again: "He has done nothing deserving of death" (Luke 23:15). Three times Pilate says it, and Jesus is still handed over anyway (Luke 23:22, 25).

So what does that teach us? Jesus isn't handed over because of anything He did. The text says the people's clamor prevailed, and Pilate sentenced that their demand be met (Luke 23:23-24). The One who is innocent ends up standing under the sentence, and that is the heart of this passage.

Then there's Barabbas, who was in prison for insurrection and murder, and he walks out free while Jesus is handed over (Luke 23:19, 25). Jesus said He came to give His life as a ransom for many (Mark 10:45). I think Barabbas gives us a small picture of that, the innocent One standing where a guilty man had been, and I think it's meant to land on us too. Hold that, baker, because this story is NOT done.
